extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on attacker-controlled body — Remote code execution on the application server [verified: pickle.loads on raw request.body/blob GET param behind only a static shared token, no allowlisting — RCE.]

Code injection via eval() of user-supplied expression — Arbitrary Python expression execution, likely sandbox escape leading to RCE [verified: eval() on user GET expr with empty __builtins__ is a known-bypassable sandbox; arbitrary expression execution reaches an attacker-controlled sink.]

Server-side template injection via Jinja2 Template from user input — Remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox escape / SSTI gadgets [verified: GET 'fragment' string-concatenated into Jinja2 Template and rendered — direct SSTI/RCE.]

Unvalidated client-controlled payroll ledger state/amount manipulation — Attacker can force a payroll ledger entry into an 'approved' state and set an arbitrary balance/limit via a single request, bypassing the intended approval workflow and enabling fraudulent payroll adjustments [verified: Client-supplied amount/state applied directly to ledger balance/state with no validation or workflow/persistence check — business logic bypass of approval flow.]

Path traversal plus plaintext SSN/card number written to disk — Arbitrary file write outside intended directory and persistent plaintext storage of sensitive PII/PAN data [verified: ref param unsanitized in path join plus plaintext SSN/card write — traversal and sensitive data exposure combined.]

Sensitive PII/card data written to disk in plaintext with path-controllable filename — Plaintext SSN/card data persisted on disk; combined with path traversal in 'ref' can write outside intended directory [verified: Duplicate of idx 6, plaintext SSN/card write plus traversal via ref.]

SSRF via unvalidated 'endpoint' parameter — Server-side request forgery to internal services / cloud metadata (e.g. 169.254.169.254), internal port scanning, data exfiltration [verified: urllib.request.urlopen on unchecked GET 'endpoint' with response reflected back — classic SSRF oracle.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make authenticated/credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses [verified: Origin header reflected verbatim into ACAO plus ACAC true — any origin gets credentialed cross-origin access.]

Path traversal leading to arbitrary file write — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, potential RCE via overwriting application code or config [verified: BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name with unsanitized GET 'name' and arbitrary write of request.body — path traversal to arbitrary file write.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF via external entity fetch, potential DoS via billion-laughs [verified: XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) parses raw request.body — classic XXE, file disclosure/SSRF.]

Privilege escalation via client-controlled cookie/header — Attacker sets a cookie/header to obtain elevated 'lead' access to payroll/casework functionality [verified: Privilege decided solely from client-supplied cookie/header equality check, no server-side identity/role verification.]

Privilege escalation via client-controlled cookie/header badge — Attacker grants themselves elevated payroll/casework access by simply sending a cookie or header value [verified: Duplicate of idx 10, badge cookie/header equality with no identity check.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized MongoDB query — Unauthorized data read from the ops MongoDB collection, potential JS injection via $where [verified: payload['filter'] or whole payload passed unvalidated to find_one() — full NoSQL operator injection.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — An attacker who knows the fallback value can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens, leading to full account takeover if the app is ever run without DJANGO_SECRET_KEY set [verified: SECRET_KEY genuinely falls back to the public literal 'dev-only-change-me' with no other safeguard, allowing session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery if the env var is unset.]

DEBUG mode defaults to True in production settings — Verbose Django debug pages leak source code, local variables, SECRET_KEY-adjacent config and stack traces to any user who triggers an unhandled exception [verified: DEBUG defaults to True (line 9) with no override required, so any unhandled exception in a fresh deployment leaks verbose stack traces, source, and settings to unauthenticated users.]

Sensitive data and Authorization header written to logs — Credentials and compensation data exposed to anyone with log access [verified: logger.warning logs full raw body and Authorization header verbatim at WARNING — credential/PII leakage to logs.]

Sensitive data (auth header, payroll body) written to logs — Credentials and sensitive payroll data leak into log files/aggregators accessible to broader staff or third-party log services [verified: Duplicate of idx 15, logs body and auth header verbatim.]

Open redirect via unvalidated 'lane' parameter — Phishing / credential harvesting by redirecting authenticated ops callers to attacker-controlled sites [verified: redirect(next_url) uses raw GET 'lane' with no allow-list/same-origin check — open redirect.]

Weak, brute-forceable verifier code with no rate limiting — Attacker can brute-force the 4-digit verifier to pass identity verification [verified: Hardcoded 4-digit verifier dict with no rate limiting; distinguishable 404/403/200 responses enable brute force.]

Weak/guessable verifier code with no rate limiting enabling brute force — Attacker can brute-force the 4-digit verifier to pass this identity check [verified: Duplicate of idx 14, differing status codes plus hardcoded short verifier enable brute force.]

Hardcoded, brute-forceable verifier codes gating ops handle — Brute-force bypass of this access check within seconds; secret exposed in source control [verified: Duplicate of idx 14/21, hardcoded brute-forceable 4-digit codes in source with no rate limiting.]

Weak PRNG used for generated code/token — Predictable tokens/codes could be guessed or brute-forced by an attacker [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) used to build a 'code' intended as a security token — predictable given state recovery.]

Weak PRNG (random.choice) used to generate security-sensitive code — Predictable tokens/nonces could be brute-forced or predicted, undermining any security purpose they serve [verified: Duplicate of idx 13, random module used for security-sensitive code generation.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept/tamper with data sent to the partner endpoint [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() used for outbound HTTPS call — disables cert/hostname verification, MITM risk.]

TLS certificate verification disabled for outbound request — Man-in-the-middle interception/tampering of outbound HTTPS traffic [verified: Duplicate of idx 11, unverified TLS context for outbound request.]

Missing Secure flag on session/CSRF cookies — Session and CSRF cookies can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP and intercepted via network MITM, enabling session hijacking [verified: Only HTTPONLY flags are set for session/CSRF cookies; SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE, and SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT are absent from settings.py, so cookies can be sent over plain HTTP despite the SSL proxy header setting.]

IDOR: Manager can reject any employee's compensation request, not just direct reports — A manager can maliciously reject compensation requests for employees outside their team, disrupting payroll workflows and denying legitimate raises/bonuses for arbitrary employees company-wide. [verified: views.py:248 checks only role in {HR_ADMIN, MANAGER} with no manager==employee.manager scoping for reject, unlike the manager_approve branch on line 241, so any MANAGER can reject any employee's request.]

Hardcoded default password for bulk-imported employee accounts — Anyone who learns/guesses the fixed default password 'ChangeMe123!' can log in as any freshly-imported employee before they change their password, gaining access to that employee's HR/payroll data and any role permissions granted to the account [verified: import_employees() hardcodes user.set_password("ChangeMe123!") for every newly created bulk-imported account with no forced reset/expiry flag, a static guessable credential shared across accounts.]

CSV formula injection via employee-editable name fields in payroll export — Formula execution / data exfiltration or command execution on the workstation of the HR/Payroll staff member who opens the exported CSV in a spreadsheet application, using a payload planted by a low-privileged employee [verified: User.first_name/last_name are attacker-controlled via the employee profile form and flow unsanitized into csv.writer at views.py:487/503-504, enabling formula injection when opened in spreadsheet software; no escaping/sanitization present.]

Verbose error disclosure of internal file paths — Discloses internal server filesystem layout, aiding further attacks such as the path traversal in adjacent endpoints [verified: Exception message embeds raw lot_ref and BASE_EXPORT_DIR path returned in JSON — internal path disclosure.]

Security headers explicitly disabled — Weakens defense-in-depth against XSS for responses served via this endpoint [verified: X-XSS-Protection:0 and empty CSP explicitly set — genuine but defense-in-depth weakening, low impact on JSON responses.]
